Here's the practical problem this grouping solves. Post-treatment Lyme disease syndrome or post-Ebola syndrome are, individually, rare enough and scattered enough that a single hospital might see only a handful of cases a year, nowhere near enough to run a rigorous clinical trial or the genetic and immunological studies needed to understand what's happening in the body. But long COVID arrived suddenly, infecting hundreds of millions of people worldwide, with a meaningful share still symptomatic years later. That scale brought research funding and infrastructure the smaller conditions never had, including large federally coordinated cohort studies. The strategy behind IACI is to test hypotheses where the numbers and the funding exist, then ask whether those findings transfer to the rarer, under-resourced conditions.
